ideas.title: A top that floats over a stone ring
ideas.goal: The player spins a magnetised top over a ring of lodestone and lets go: if the spin is fast enough and the top's weight is right, it hovers in the air, wobbling, and falls when it slows. The game is the tuning: add or file off little copper washers until it floats, then beat your hover time. Too light and it flies off sideways, too heavy and it sinks.
ideas.toward: Fields and rigid bodies together, as the motor needs: a body spinning in a real field, with nothing holding it but the force and torque from em.jl. Earnshaw says a still magnet can never float, so if it floats, the physics did it.
ideas.idea: physics/top.jl's full rigid top (it exists: profile, inertia, precession) gets em.jl's force and torque from a ring magnet mesh (any mesh works). Floating needs the gyroscopic stability window, a few percent in weight and a band of spin, so it can only come from the solve, never a script. Watching: a small top spinning in mid-air above a dark ring, slowly precessing, then wobbling wider and dropping.
ideas.form: A new spot by the tops board in Jump in (hold 1 to spin, 6/7 to add or file a washer); a film of one float from the spin to the drop, with the hover time.

ideas.title: Three stones, one pendulum, the friends bet
ideas.goal: A spike hangs on a thread over three magnet stones in the sand. The friends each pick a stone, the player pulls the spike back and lets go: it swings, hesitates, wobbles between them and settles on one, and that friend cheers. A tiny change in where you let go changes the winner, so you learn to cheat and never quite can.
ideas.toward: Unplanned outcomes from real fields: the friends' game is decided by the field solver alone, with three magnets acting on one induced magnet at once.
ideas.idea: The spike is a pendulum (a rod on a thread, gravity, air drag) magnetised by the three stones through physics/softiron.jl, the force from em.jl's charges. Each finish leaves a coloured pebble on the sand where it was let go, so over days the friends' games draw the pendulum's fractal map of basins. Watching: the swing, three creatures leaning in, the pebble map growing.
ideas.form: A creature game in the north beach plugin with bets and cheers; a film of three swings and the pebble map.

ideas.title: Shake a stone through a coil, the needle kicks
ideas.goal: The player pushes the magnet stone through a hoop of wound copper wire; a compass needle beside the hoop kicks each time, harder the faster you shove, and backwards when you pull it out. Shaking fast enough warms a hair-thin wire joined to the coil. You get good at the rhythm that makes the biggest kick.
ideas.toward: Induction, the end of the road (the motor run backwards makes a lamp), from the same fields: the current is made by the stone, not typed in.
ideas.idea: The flux through each turn of the coil is integrated from the stone's real field (em.jl) every frame; EMF = -dPhi/dt; the current = EMF / the wire's resistance from its length and copper's resistivity; the coil's own field (Biot-Savart over its turns) turns the floating compass needle that exists. Watching: Lumi swinging the stone, the needle jerking.
ideas.form: A coil and compass by the compass bowl in Jump in; a film of shoves and kicks.

ideas.title: A magnet that falls slowly through copper
ideas.goal: The player drops the magnet stone's small chips down tubes: a hollow reed, a rolled iron sheet, a rolled copper sheet. In the reed it drops, in iron it sticks, in copper it sinks slowly as if through honey. Then guessing games: what do the friends' things do (a shell, a brass bell)?
ideas.toward: Currents that the field makes in any conductor (eddy currents) push back on the magnet: conductivity from the materials table decides, the general solver for every metal.
ideas.idea: The tube wall is a mesh of conductor patches; the moving magnet's changing field drives currents in them (a thin-sheet eddy solve: loop currents on the patches with their resistance and mutual inductance), whose field pushes back on the falling chip. Watching: the copper chip easing down the tube while the friends crane in.
ideas.form: A table of tubes on the beach in Jump in; a film of three drops side by side.

ideas.title: The friends try to steal Lumi's iron tail
ideas.goal: Lumi walks with a chain of spikes hanging from the stone; the friends chase and grab the bottom spike. Where the chain breaks follows from the field: grab low and one spike comes off, yank hard near the stone and the whole tail drops. The player swings and turns to keep the tail, a chase with a physical prize.
ideas.toward: Iron magnetises iron (physics/softiron.jl, solved: two hold, the third at the edge), with creatures as the forces on the chain.
ideas.idea: The chain is solved each frame (every spike's pieces together), each joint holds while its pull beats the load below it, and a creature's beak grip is a force on a spike; the chain sways as a linked pendulum. Watching: a yellow bird with a dangling iron tail and a crab hanging off its end.
ideas.form: In the magnet stone plugin, the friends' chase in Jump in; a chase film.

ideas.title: Iron sand that shows every field
ideas.goal: Black iron sand in the north beach bristles into tufts wherever any magnet comes near, the stone today and every coil and motor later. The player rakes it with the stone into lines and pictures that stay, and sees the shape of any field they build.
ideas.toward: The island's own field viewer: every later device shows its real field in the sand, nothing drawn on the screen.
ideas.idea: Thousands of grains on the GPU (Mantle kernels): each grain a small soft iron sphere magnetised by the outside field plus its close neighbours (pair forces within three grain sizes, solved by a few relaxation sweeps), so tufts come from grains chaining, as they really do. Watching: a black beard growing on the stone and dripping off when it turns.
ideas.form: A GPU particle system in the north beach plugin; a close film of tufts.
